caption: What if you chased the coldest temperature ever? Your freezer sits at about -18 °C. Dry ice, frozen carbon dioxide, is -78 °C and turns straight into fog. Earth's coldest air ever recorded was -89.2 °C at Vostok Station, Antarctica, on 21 July 1983. Liquid nitrogen boils at -196 °C, which is why Tamil Nadu and Karnataka banned it in 'smoke biscuits' in 2024: it can burn you inside, so never eat or touch it. Neptune's moon Triton is about -235 °C. The Boomerang Nebula, 5,000 light-years away, is about -272 °C, colder than the Big Bang's afterglow. In 1995 a lab cooled atoms to 170 billionths of a degree, making a Bose-Einstein condensate, named after Kolkata-born physicist S. N. Bose. In 2021 a German drop tower hit 38 trillionths of a degree above absolute zero. Plot twist: at normal pressure, helium never freezes, not even near absolute zero. Which number shocked YOU most? 👇
